claims: The Jones Act is the Merchant Marine Act of 1920.
The Jones Act is a federal statute.
The Jones Act requires goods transported by water between U.S. ports to be carried on ships that are U.S.-flagged, U.S.-built, U.S.-owned, and U.S.-crewed.
According to the Maritime Administration, Jones Act vessels must be U.S.-built.
According to the Maritime Administration, Jones Act vessels must be owned by U.S. citizens.
According to the Maritime Administration, Jones Act vessels must be at least 75% U.S.-crewed.
According to the Maritime Administration, Jones Act vessels must be U.S.-flagged.
The Jones Act was enacted after World War I.
The Jones Act significantly affects Puerto Rico, Hawaii, Alaska, and Guam.
The Secretary of Homeland Security can waive the Jones Act for reasons of national defense.
Temporary waivers of the Jones Act have been issued to lower oil and gas costs.
